video.title: watch this if you're tired of being broke

summary: A mindset-focused conversation between Chris Koerner and Shannon Gene (a reseller and content creator, speaking from Northern California) about the foundations of entrepreneurship: falling in love with problem solving, embracing fear and change, having 'delusions of grandeur' backed by action, and building a bias for action driven by curiosity and quick dopamine rewards. Koerner describes validating a private pickleball club in his metal shop with a $1.78-per-lead Facebook ad test, and Shannon Gene covers manual-before-automation lessons from Poshmark, Amazon self-publishing and obscure-parts reselling. The key takeaway is to start small, do things manually first, validate demand cheaply with math and act quickly. Few numbers are given and most are anecdotal.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; content creator, writing a book called Bias for Action, opening a private pickleball club.

speakers.name: Shannon Gene
speakers.description: Reseller and auction/eBay educator, bestselling Amazon self-published author, runs a $5/month mastermind community; former consumer electronics business owner.

ideas.name: Private pickleball club in a metal shop
ideas.one_liner: Convert an existing metal shop into a private members-only pickleball court at about $100 per month, validated with Facebook ads before spending.
ideas.customer: Pickleball players living within roughly a six mile radius of the shop
ideas.problem: Players want a private, social place to play and talk about it (implied); not explicitly stated beyond demand testing.
ideas.offer: Private pickleball club membership in a converted metal shop, possibly with an added bathroom.

pricing.notes: Planned price, not yet validated by sales.

acquisition_channels.details: Facebook ad campaign with a self-edited video shot at the shop, targeted to a six mile radius; got 2-3 leads overnight at $1.78 each.

quote.text: I paid $1.78 for each of them. Yeah. It's awesome. Like $6 30 minutes of time.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Posted a listing on Facebook Marketplace to gauge demand; a couple of messages in the first day.

ideas.delivery: Physical venue: a metal shop converted with a court and potentially a bathroom (septic system check underway). Owner-operated facility.
unit_economics_claims: Assumed close rate 5% and cost per lead up to $10-20 would still make financial sense
ideas.startup_cost: Not stated overall; $39 septic quote visit, plus ad spend of about $6 so far; owns the shop.

acquisition.how: Paid Facebook ads with local targeting can be run and optimised largely by software with occasional human creative approval.

onboarding.how: Membership sign-up and waivers can be online, but access and induction to a physical site need some human involvement.

delivery.how: Physical facility must be built, maintained, cleaned and managed by a human.

billing.how: Recurring membership billing can be fully automated via Stripe or similar.

support.how: Member queries and booking can be handled by agents, but on-site issues need a human.

uk_applicability.notes: Concept works in the UK, but needs planning permission/change of use, building regs, insurance and licensing; indoor pickleball is growing in the UK. Prices in GBP and local radius targeting would differ.

risks: Demand unvalidated beyond cheap leads; leads may not convert to paying members
Septic, bathroom, permitting and insurance costs
Koerner admits breaking his own rule of validating before spending ($39 septic visit)
Facebook leads may be low quality or geographically wrong

ideas.name: Reselling items (eBay, Facebook Marketplace, Poshmark)
ideas.one_liner: Start by selling things from your own house, then source items matching your interests, building systems as you learn.
ideas.business_model: Buy low, sell higher via online marketplaces
ideas.problem: People with no capital or experience need a low-risk way to start earning and learning.
ideas.offer: Resold goods chosen to match the reseller's interests (e.g. Blackstone grills, tools, camping, handbags).

pricing.notes: Not stated beyond examples like a $100 first sale.

acquisition_channels.details: List on eBay, Facebook Marketplace and Poshmark; on Poshmark follow thousands of targeted users a day so they notice and buy.

ideas.delivery: Seller ships physical goods they own or source; Poshmark following was done manually then automated.
unit_economics_claims: First sales from stuff at home are 'found money'
Aim for a first $100 to $1,000 to trigger motivation
ideas.startup_cost: Near zero if selling your own household items
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Fast; selling household items gives quick cash (not quantified)

acquisition.how: Listings and Poshmark-style follow automation can be tooled, though platform terms may limit it.

delivery.how: Physical sourcing, storing, packing and shipping requires humans.

support.how: Buyer messages and returns can be partly handled by agents.

uk_applicability.notes: eBay, Vinted and Facebook Marketplace work in the UK; no resale permit needed but HMRC trading allowance and platform reporting apply.

risks: Platform rule changes and account bans
Thin margins on commodity goods like iPhones

quotes.text: if you want to become a reseller, sell stuff in your house.
quotes.speaker: Shannon Gene

ideas.name: Obscure legacy parts sourcing (FAA floppy discs)
ideas.one_liner: Find institutional buyers like the FAA who need obsolete components and source them in low-competition niches.
ideas.business_model: Sourcing and reselling niche obsolete hardware at high margin
ideas.customer: Organisations maintaining old systems, e.g. the FAA
ideas.problem: Legacy systems need parts that are no longer manufactured.
ideas.offer: Sourced obsolete components such as five and a half inch floppy discs.

acquisition_channels.details: Search eBay for the FAA's buying account to see what they buy, then source those items.

unit_economics_claims: 'There's good money in that' with no margin figures

acquisition.how: Monitoring marketplaces can be tooled but finding buyers needs judgement.

uk_applicability.notes: The principle of finding obscure parts for institutions works in the UK (e.g. NHS, rail, defence legacy kit), but the FAA angle is US-specific.

risks: Idea is speculative, from one article
Demand may be tiny or irregular

quotes.text: I want to sell five and a half inch floppy discs for an FAA machine that they need to keep going.
quotes.speaker: Shannon Gene

ideas.name: Self-published Amazon book
ideas.one_liner: Turn expertise or failed project content into a bestselling self-published book for royalties and authority.
ideas.business_model: Book royalties plus authority for other offers
ideas.problem: Authors want passive income and credibility from existing knowledge.
ideas.offer: A self-published book on Amazon, written from lived experience.

acquisition_channels.details: Amazon's marketplace; hired a coach and learned how publishers hack becoming a bestseller.

ideas.delivery: Writing and publishing a book; digital distribution by Amazon.
unit_economics_claims: $800 and $500 royalty payments from two books
ideas.startup_cost: Cost of coach and software, not stated

acquisition.how: Amazon search and ads with some optimisation.

delivery.how: AI can draft and format; human oversight of quality and facts needed.

uk_applicability.notes: Amazon KDP operates in the UK; royalties are taxable income.

risks: Royalties can be small and uncertain
Low-quality AI books face platform scrutiny (my view)

ideas.one_liner: Using viral short-form video as bait to funnel people into newsletter, podcast, community and offers.
ideas.business_model: Audience funnel with newsletter, podcast, mastermind and other offers
ideas.problem: People want business ideas and actionable playbooks.
ideas.offer: Free videos, a weekly tactical newsletter, a podcast and community with a 'whistle, workhorse and whale' offer structure.

price_points.label: Shannon Gene's mastermind, close to 500 members

pricing.notes: Koerner's own offers are not priced here.

acquisition_channels.details: Short-form videos get over 100 million views a month; ideas serve as bait.

quote.text: My short form videos get over 100 million views a month
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Creator-produced videos, email newsletter and podcasts.

acquisition.how: AI can help script, edit and repurpose content, but personality-led content needs a human.

delivery.how: Personality-based content hard to fully automate.

quotes.text: The ideas are like the bait, you know? That's what people get.

ideas.name: Auction and pallet buying business
ideas.one_liner: Buy pallets at automated auctions using strict spreadsheet maximum bids, accepting that most bids lose.
ideas.business_model: Buy pallets at auction and resell for profit
ideas.offer: Disciplined auction buying with a pre-set maximum bid.

acquisition_channels.details: Online auction platforms where you enter a high bid and walk away.

ideas.delivery: Win pallets, then store and resell physical goods.
unit_economics_claims: You'll lose around 80% of auctions; the 20% you win is the money
tools: Online auction software with automatic bidding

acquisition.how: Auto-bidding and spreadsheet-based evaluation can be automated.

delivery.how: Physical pickup, storage, listing and shipping.

uk_applicability.notes: UK liquidation and pallet auctions exist (e.g. returns pallets); VAT and buyer premiums apply.

quotes.text: If your spreadsheet tells you you can pay $3,500 for that pallet of stuff, you put your 3500 bucks in and leave

ideas.offer: Smoked brisket sold from a parking lot or similar site.

ideas.delivery: Cook and sell food in person.
unit_economics_claims: Speaker admires the brisket money but gives no figures
ideas.startup_cost: Speaker wonders how much investment; not stated

acquisition.how: Social content and pre-orders possible but local following requires presence.

delivery.how: Cooking and serving food is physical.

uk_applicability.notes: Street food requires council trading licence, food hygiene registration and pitch permission in the UK.

tactics.name: Validate demand cheaply with a local Facebook ad before spending
steps: Shoot a short video of the space
Edit it yourself to avoid friction
Create a Facebook ad campaign in about 10 minutes
Target a tight radius (six miles was chosen over five or seven)
Check cost per lead and ask leads follow-up questions like how often they'd play and how far they live
Extrapolate: stress-test at $10-20 per lead and 5% close rate

quote.text: I need to put Facebook ads up to see if there's any demand for this.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Learn manually before automating
steps: Do the task by hand first (e.g. follow people on Poshmark)
Observe which actions and buyer types lead to sales
Build a system from what you learned
Then automate it

quote.text: we're going to learn how to do this manually. I'm going to teach you how to do it manually.
quote.speaker: Shannon Gene

tactics.name: Buy with math, sell with emotion
steps: Decide a maximum price from a spreadsheet
Enter the max bid in the auction software and walk away
Optionally use an odd number like 3505
Use emotional storytelling and video when selling

quote.text: you need to buy with math and sell with emotion, right?
quote.speaker: Shannon Gene

tactics.name: Whistle, workhorse and whale offer ladder
steps: Create an attention-getting whistle offer
Make a workhorse offer that earns the daily bread-and-butter income
Add a whale high-end offer for fewer buyers

quote.text: You you need a whistle for your business. What gets attention and then you get people in
quote.speaker: Shannon Gene

tactics.name: Start reselling from your interests
steps: Ask what the person likes (sports, camping, cooking, tools)
Find products in that interest, e.g. Blackstone grills
Find where to buy them and sell online
Use the early cash wins as motivation

tactics.name: Act on curiosity within the hour
steps: When a question or idea appears that can be answered in an hour, do it right away
Use notes and reminders apps for the rest
Look for a quick reward such as a first sale or lead

tactics.name: Drop conversation hooks and ask questions
steps: Mention interesting things you have done and let people ask
Ask others about their business and how they make money
Connect more with people who ask questions back

warnings.warning: If you stay in a bad rut and change nothing, nothing improves; change something physical or behavioural.

quote.text: if you're stuck in the suck, right? And you don't do anything different, you're going to be in the suck forever.
quote.speaker: Shannon Gene

warnings.warning: Don't skip the manual stage and jump straight to automation or delegation; people who do never learn business fundamentals.

quote.text: if you skip that and go right to this fully automated part, I don't I don't think you value it as much.
quote.speaker: Shannon Gene

warnings.warning: Don't let emotion drive auction bids; stick to your pre-set maximum.

quote.text: Don't sit there and go, "Oh, oh, no. I'm going to I'm just another hundred, just no, because that's emotion.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: You can ruin things you love by monetizing them.

quote.text: you can ruin things you love by monetizing them.
quote.speaker: Shannon Gene

warnings.warning: Don't talk too much about what you're going to do; talk about what you've done, or people see you as a blowhard.

lessons.lesson: Treat problems as the job, not as barriers; every business creates new problems, so expect and enjoy solving them.

quote.text: you should fall in love with problem solving because that's your job every single day.
quote.speaker: Shannon Gene

lessons.lesson: Start small and low-risk (e.g. selling household items) so early wins build confidence and a dopamine feedback loop.

quote.text: the dopamine is the cash you get boom I made a hundred bucks
quote.speaker: Shannon Gene

lessons.lesson: Validate demand with cheap tests before spending money, then stress-test the numbers with pessimistic assumptions.
Delusions of grandeur are useful if bolted onto action; ideas alone are bait, execution and tools are what matter.

quote.text: you have to bolt it on to action
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Learn the fundamentals by hand before automating or outsourcing; manual work reveals the system you later automate.
Keep businesses simple and focus on how much of each dollar reaches your pocket.
Change something when stuck: routine and habit lock in bad situations, so deliberately vary physical environment and routine.

quote.text: Nothing changes if nothing changes.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Niche, obscure products avoid competition and preserve margin compared with commodity goods.
Strategic ignorance of negative comments can help creators keep publishing consistently.
Follow strategic people in business so your feed generates curiosity and ideas that prompt action.

evidence_quality.rationale: Mostly a mindset and motivation conversation with anecdotes and few numbers. The only concrete first-hand figures are the $1.78 lead cost, planned $100 membership and Amazon royalties of a few hundred dollars; the pickleball idea has not launched. Most other ideas are mentions.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Koerner promotes his newsletter/podcast (tkopod.com) and a book in progress; Shannon Gene runs a $5/month mastermind and teaches reselling.
